samples.summary: undo/redo neutering assertions are vacuous — the underlying store has no history, so a forwarded undo/redo would pass identically
samples.evidence: In 'neuters every write path' (read-only.test.ts:35-48) the store is a fresh `MemNoteStore('hello')` and every write goes through the neutered view, so the raw store's undo stack is empty. `MemNoteStore.undo()` returns `null` when the stack is empty (memory.ts:173-179), so `expect(view.undo()).toBeNull()` / `expect(view.redo()).toBeNull()` hold whether or not `HISTORY_METHODS` neuters them. Deleting `undo`/`redo` from HISTORY_METHODS in read-only.ts:35 (i.e. moving them to the reader allowlist, or having a future refactor forward them) would not fail any test. No test anywhere seeds history on the raw store (e.g. `store.editText(...)`) and then asserts `view.undo()` neither reverts the text nor pops the stack — the closest is the first test, which calls `store.undo()` on the RAW store deliberately. A forwarded undo on a viewer mount is a real CRDT write that reverts document content.

samples.summary: setLocalSelection / recordSelectionForHistory neutering is asserted only by observations that cannot see them
samples.evidence: read-only.test.ts:38-46 calls `view.setLocalSelection(1, 2)` and `view.recordSelectionForHistory({anchor:0,head:0})` but the only assertions afterwards are `store.getText() === 'hello'` and `store.canUndo() === false`. Neither method touches text or the undo stack in `MemNoteStore` (memory.ts:167-171, 204-210) — they only update the private `currentSelection` / `batchAfterSelection`. So the test passes unchanged if `setLocalSelection` and `recordSelectionForHistory` were forwarded to the real store. This is a behaviour the diff deliberately changes (read-only.ts:132-137: a viewer's caret is no longer published, and on the Yorkie store that publish is a `doc.update` write); it currently has no assertion that can fail. It is observable with the existing store: `view.setLocalSelection(...)` followed by `store.editText(...)` then `store.undo()` returns the pinned pre-edit selection (memory.ts:92-94, 178).

samples.summary: No test fails if the new `readOnly ? readOnlyNoteStore(noteStore) : noteStore` wrapping in initialize() is removed
samples.evidence: editor.ts now wraps the store on read-only mounts, but the existing read-only editor tests (editor.test.ts:36-63 'lets no write reach the store on a read-only mount', :223 'leaves history unbound') already passed before this change — they assert via `vi.spyOn(store,'editText')`/`undo` not being called, which the pre-existing view-level gates already guaranteed. No test asserts that the store handed to `noteStoreFacet` / returned via the engine is the guarded one (e.g. by pulling the store out of the facet and calling `editText` on it, or by having a plugin path write directly). The wrapping line is therefore untested integration glue; deleting it leaves the suite green.

verdict.reason: Verified as described. In 'neuters every write path' (read-only.test.ts:32-47) the store is a fresh MemNoteStore('hello') and every write is routed through the proxy, all of which are neutered (read-only.ts:117-138), so the raw undo stack stays empty. MemNoteStore.undo()/redo() return null on an empty stack (memory.ts:173-187), so `expect(view.undo()).toBeNull()` / `toBeNull()` for redo — and `store.canUndo() === false` — hold identically whether undo/redo are neutered by HISTORY_METHODS (read-only.ts:35) or forwarded via the reader-allowlist bind at read-only.ts:118. The assertions only exclude the generic void-noop bucket (undefined), not forwarding, which is the access-control behavior at issue. No other test seeds history on the raw store and asserts view.undo() is inert: the only readOnlyNoteStore tests are in this file, and read-only.test.ts:26-27 deliberately calls store.editText/store.undo() on the RAW store for the subscription assertion. Impact is real because YorkieNoteStore.undo() calls doc.history.undo() (yorkie-note-store.ts:275-281), a CRDT write that would revert document content on a viewer mount — a silently weakened write guard shipping untested. In-lane (vacuous assertion presented as coverage) and major.

verdict.reason: Verified as described. read-only.test.ts:32-47 (the test named 'neuters every write path') calls view.recordSelectionForHistory({anchor:0,head:0}) and view.setLocalSelection(1,2), but its only surviving assertions are store.getText() === 'hello' and store.canUndo() === false. In MemNoteStore, recordSelectionForHistory (memory.ts:167-171) and setLocalSelection (memory.ts:204-210) mutate only currentSelection / batchAfterSelection and never touch text, undoStack, or redoStack — and because read-only.ts:121-130 runs the batch body without entering the store's real batch(), store.batchDepth stays 0, so even a forwarded recordSelectionForHistory would only set currentSelection. Both assertions therefore hold unchanged if these two methods were forwarded to the real store, so the test cannot fail if this neutering regresses. read-only.ts:131-137 shows the neutering of setLocalSelection is a deliberate behavior of this wrapper (publishing a caret is a doc.update write on the Yorkie store), and read-only.ts:57-61 notes the server-side webhook ships in shadow mode, making this wrapper the write boundary. A distinguishing assertion is readily available with the existing store: a forwarded setLocalSelection(1,2) followed by store.editText(...) then store.undo() would return {anchor:1,head:2} rather than null (memory.ts:91-94, 173-179). I grepped all test files for readOnlyNoteStore and readOnly: read-only.test.ts is the only test of this wrapper, and nothing in packages/notes/src/view/editor.test.ts or the frontend covers caret suppression on a read-only mount. This is fake coverage of a write-boundary guard, presented under a test claiming to cover every write path — in lane and blocking.
